name: obd2-mcp
description: Read trouble codes, freeze frame, live sensors and readiness monitors from your car through an ELM327 adapter. Starts with a mock vehicle, so no car is needed to try it.
long_description:
Lets Claude read OBD-II data from your own car through an inexpensive ELM327-compatible USB, Bluetooth (serial) or WiFi adapter: stored and pending trouble codes, the freeze frame, live sensors (and how they change over up to 30 seconds while parked), readiness monitors and VIN. A diagnostic report tool collects the evidence for a workshop discussion and can compare two reports (for example before and after a test drive or a repair), and guided prompts cover a warning light, a workshop handover, a used-car check and readiness before an emissions inspection. Guides and the latest report can be attached from the obd2-mcp resources.

The default connection is a simulated vehicle with a stored P0420, so you can try every tool without hardware. To use a real adapter, plug it in, turn the ignition on and ask Claude to connect: it finds a USB or Bluetooth adapter with `find_adapter` and, after asking you, connects with `use_adapter` until Claude Desktop restarts. To keep the connection, set **Adapter connection** in the extension settings.

Results are observations, not a diagnosis. Clearing codes on a real vehicle is disabled. Real-vehicle and real-adapter compatibility has not yet been verified by the project; start with read-only checks while safely parked.

tools.name: connection_status
tools.description: Check the adapter identity and port voltage.

tools.name: find_adapter
tools.description: Find a USB or Bluetooth ELM327 adapter automatically.

tools.name: use_adapter
tools.description: Connect this session to the found adapter, without editing settings.

tools.name: list_serial_ports
tools.description: Find the serial: connection value for a USB or Bluetooth adapter.

tools.name: read_dtcs
tools.description: Read stored and pending trouble codes and the check-engine light state.

tools.name: read_permanent_dtcs
tools.description: Read permanent trouble codes that remain after codes are cleared.

tools.name: read_supported_pids
tools.description: Discover which live sensors the vehicle advertises.

tools.name: watch_live_data
tools.description: Watch up to four live sensors for up to 30 seconds while parked.

tools.name: read_live_data
tools.description: Read live sensors such as RPM, coolant temperature and fuel trims.

tools.name: read_freeze_frame
tools.description: Read the engine conditions recorded when a code was set.

tools.name: read_diagnostic_report
tools.description: Collect codes, freeze frame, live data and readiness in one evidence report.

tools.name: compare_diagnostic_reports
tools.description: Compare two diagnostic reports to see what changed, without contacting the vehicle.

tools.name: clear_dtcs
tools.description: Clear trouble codes (destructive; disabled for real vehicles by default).

connection.title: Adapter connection
connection.description: mock for the simulated car (default). For a USB or paired Bluetooth adapter use serial:<port>, for example serial:COM3 or serial:/dev/ttyUSB0 (ask Claude to find your adapter). For a WiFi adapter use tcp:<host>:<port>, commonly tcp:192.168.0.10:35000.

mock_scenario.title: Mock scenario
mock_scenario.description: Used only with mock: catalyst (P0420, default), healthy, misfire (P0301), lean (P0171), evap (P0456), cleared (codes cleared recently: no stored codes, but a permanent P0420 and incomplete monitors) or partial (P0128 with unsupported sensors and no freeze frame). Synthetic examples, not diagnoses.

baud.title: Serial baud rate
baud.description: Used only with serial: connections. Most ELM327 adapters use 38400; some need 115200.
